subject: Phased rollout: usage safety net & overage terms
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Stevens <j.stevens@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Phased rollout: usage safety net & overage terms

Jordan —

Great chatting earlier. As we scope the MAP and the evaluation plan, ACME's staged rollout poses a few commercial questions our finance and delivery teams need covered before we finalize timelines:

1) Safety net during evaluation: can we agree on a soft-cap with automatic alerts during the first 6 weeks of ramp and a clearly priced temporary burst option if you exceed it?

2) Overage vs. emergency burst: we typically provide a two-tier approach — a 'soft cap' with no hard enforcement (alerts + throttling suggestions) and an 'emergency burst' (manual approval, higher per-token rate). We'd like to put those exact numbers in the MAP so procurement can sign.

3) Rate card snapshot: we'll attach the June ratecard and a draft MAP that recommends staged commits tied to milestones (PO, staging success, 1M usable tokens). Please call out any target ceilings that are non-negotiable for ACME.

Attached: proposed_MAP_v2.pdf, ratecard_snapshot_Jun25.xlsx, evaluation_schedule_v1.xlsx

High level ask: can you confirm by EOD Thursday which safety-net level ACME is comfortable with (soft cap at 50k tokens/day with alerts / hard cap at 200k tokens/day / emergency burst up to 500k at elevated rate)? Once we have that, I can escalate for a short-term credit if you need it for the pilot.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_MAP_v2.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: ratecard_snapshot_Jun25.xlsx (Excel)]
From: Jordan Stevens <j.stevens@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Phased rollout: usage safety net & overage terms

Ben —

Thanks for the summary and the docs. Quick answers from our side:

- We absolutely need a safety net while the feature is in pilot. Our procurement team wants a hard ceiling for automated enforcement during the first 30 days, with the option to request temporary increases.
- For the evaluation, can we do: hard cap = 250k tokens/day, soft alert at 60% utilization, and emergency burst up to 600k tokens/day (requires manual approval and we accept a higher overage rate)?
- We will need the exact overage rate to be called out in the MAP (per-token delta) so it clears procurement. Can you propose the delta vs standard rate?

Also looping in Priya (ops) — Priya, any SSO or network whitelist items we should flag for Redwood's private deployment during the test?

Jordan
Jordan Stevens
Director, AI Integrations
ACME Enterprises
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Stevens <j.stevens@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Phased rollout: usage safety net & overage terms

Jordan —

Appreciate the clarity. We can agree to the hard cap and soft-alert structure you outlined. Proposed commercial guardrails:

- Soft alert: 60% of daily hard cap (we'll send automated email + Slack alert)
- Hard cap: 250k tokens/day during initial 30-day pilot (requests above this will be blocked unless manually approved)
- Emergency burst: up to 600k tokens/day for up to 48 hours with prior written approval; emergency burst rate = standard list rate + 65% premium (we'll show exact numbers in the MAP PDF)
- Short-term credit: Redwood can offer a one-time evaluation credit equal to 40% of the pilot month's overage charges (applies only if usage exceeds hard cap and you sign the PO within 14 days of pilot end).

I've updated the draft MAP (attached) and included a redlined ratecard snapshot. If that delta premium looks acceptable, we can move to a DocuSign for the pilot addendum.

Next steps: 1) Jordan/Priya to confirm SSO/whitelist items 2) ACME to confirm burst acceptance and 3) Redwood to circulate DocuSign for the pilot addendum.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_MAP_v2.pdf (PDF) — updated]
[Attachment: ratecard_snapshot_Jun25.xlsx (Excel) — redlined]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-01T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: ACME pilot guardrails — approval ask for eval credit and emergency rate

Team —

ACME accepted the hard-cap + emergency burst model. They specifically asked for the overage premium number in the MAP. I proposed standard +65% for emergency bursts; I also offered a one-time evaluation credit (40%) to reduce friction for pilot overruns if they sign quickly.

Can finance sign off on:
- 40% one-time eval credit (applies only to overage charges during pilot and only if PO signed within 14 days of pilot end)
- Emergency burst premium at +65% of standard per-token rate (visible in ratecard)

If yes, I'll prep DocuSign and send the pilot addendum. If you want to push for a lower premium in exchange for a higher committed post-pilot capacity, we can make that offer in the MAP.

Ben
From: Jordan Stevens <j.stevens@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Phased rollout: usage safety net & overage terms — Confirmed

Ben / Marissa —

Thanks — confirmed from ACME side: we accept the hard-cap at 250k/day, soft alert at 60%, and emergency burst up to 600k/day at the proposed premium. We appreciate Redwood offering the evaluation credit — procurement will expect that in writing in the pilot addendum.

Next: Priya will share SSO and network whitelist details by tomorrow. We'll also route the pilot addendum to procurement once we see the DocuSign with the exact numbers.

Jordan
